lines: YTD'26 includes a one-time tax expense of $1.7 billion due to the revocation of ACRA's election to be subject to the Government of Bermuda's Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 as a result of updated guidance issued during the first quarter, which led to the recognition of a full valuation allowance against the Bermuda deferred tax assets, as previously disclosed.

desk.headline: Record fee earnings up 23%, adjusted EPS $2.07; GAAP loss of $1.1bn on Athene marks; 2026 growth targets reaffirmed

other.label: ANI per share excl. notable items

results: Fee related earnings hit a record $802m, up 23%, as management fees rose 18% and capital solutions fees 37% to $290m; FRE margin 58.4%.
Spread earnings from Athene fell 3% to $844m; excluding the annual assumption review they rose 7% to a record $909m.
Adjusted net income was $1.29bn, or $2.07 a share (vs $2.17); GAAP showed a $1.06bn loss as higher rates hit Athene's investment marks, and GAAP revenue fell to $4.7bn from $9.8bn.
Assets under management reached $1.07tn, up 18%, with $53bn of inflows and record origination of $114bn in the quarter.
Apollo bought back $143m of shares in the quarter and declared a $0.5625 dividend.

guidance.summary: The release gives no numeric outlook. On the call, as reported, Apollo reaffirmed 2026 targets of 20%+ FRE growth and 10% SRE growth, guided Q4 SRE to about $1bn and set first 2027 targets.

points: Management pointed to record origination as its growth engine and said core earnings are set for a strong end to 2026.
Fee growth is slowing: management fee growth eased to 18% from the low 20s earlier in the year, and the 2027 target of 15%+ partly reflects selling MFIC fees to Ares.
Apollo plans about $350m of investment spending over two years, plus software write-offs.
The tone on markets was defensive: high valuations, tight credit spreads, AI-related concentration in investment-grade debt and rates biased higher.
Coming up: a minority stake in Mubadala Capital closing late in Q4, a new European credit platform and daily pricing across the credit book.
call.source: Call coverage: Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 3 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Q4 spread earnings reach the ~$1bn guide.
The pace of fee growth as investment spending rises.
Athene's alternative returns against the 11% long-term assumption, and GAAP marks if rates keep rising.

sources.title: Apollo misses by a hair as record origination meets decelerating fee growth and a costly build-out — Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 3 Nov 2026
